params.description: Required non-null object in this edit command's parameter grammar; query capabilities.list {command: EDIT_COMMAND} for bounds, quantities and fields. Child commands carry no separate protocol envelope/key/revision. Batch staging overrides live actuation/completion semantics.

name.description: Required non-null name, not all whitespace, 1–80 UTF-8 bytes including surrounding whitespace. Stored verbatim if final document content adds an undo entry.

preconditions: Common protocol/revision/document/actor/retry guards apply before the command; one outer mutation guard and key cover the entire operation

Required non-null name and 1–100 edits; each edit needs a nonempty allowed command and parameter object. No nested batches, file work, queries, run controls, history, pin/display preferences or general experiment-settings command

Edits validate in order against cloned graph/settings/drawing/selection/lifetime IDs. Later edits can use earlier explicit IDs, wiring and staged values; each intermediate edit must be structurally valid, but the circuit need not be electrically complete
effects: Successful admission advances command revision even for unchanged final content. Successful retries return independently owned original snapshots before new guard checks, not a fresh snapshot or another edit
Saved-file association/baselines and kept captured assets are independent of schematic history. Dirty flags compare current contents with the latest saved baseline, not the existence of an undo entry

Any rejected child discards all staged graph/settings/drawing/selection and ID reservations; preserves public state, history, physical readings/run/time and files. Error messages identify the 1-based edit index when child execution fails

Commits staged graph/transient settings/selection/drawing/ID reservations once. A final graph/settings change adds one named actor/revision-attributed undo entry, clears redo and follows ordinary electrical versus geometry-only edit behavior

A batch with unchanged final graph/settings adds no history entry and preserves redo/accepted physics. It can still consume lifetime IDs for components/wires created then deleted, change editing selection/drawing and advance the outer command revision

Switch/wiper edits are staged startup configuration, not live queued actuation. Sampling Fit uses preceding staged values. Finite and ideal-square timing bounds use staged experiment settings. All selected children reuse their ordinary value/geometry/quantity validation
Undo restores graph/settings/pins/display/example contents only; it does not release IDs from a successful batch or restore editing selection/drawing, file association, kept data or live time/charge

errors.when: Malformed/unknown/duplicate fields or command-specific domain validation

completion.mode: immediate schematic/history commit; electrical edits use existing startup/paused stale rules

allow_other_actor.description: Optional omitted/null/false refuses a tip owned by another actor. True acknowledges another actor only after any exact-tip guard matches; it does not bypass context guards.

expected_entry_revision.description: Optional omitted/null adds no exact-tip guard; supplied uint64 must equal the chosen undo_entry/redo_entry.command_revision. Zero is an actual comparison, not a disable sentinel.

preconditions: Common protocol/revision/document/actor/retry guards apply before the command; one outer mutation guard and key cover the entire operation
After common guards and parameter decoding: requested stack nonempty, optional exact tip revision matches, then original tip actor equals caller or allow_other_actor=true
effects: Successful admission advances command revision even for unchanged final content. Successful retries return independently owned original snapshots before new guard checks, not a fresh snapshot or another edit
Saved-file association/baselines and kept captured assets are independent of schematic history. Dirty flags compare current contents with the latest saved baseline, not the existence of an undo entry

Restores one graph/transient-settings/pinned/display/example history state and moves the counterpart to the opposite stack under the original name/actor/entry revision, even when another actor explicitly acknowledges it

History is session-local and bounded, not loaded from project/recovery files. A later changed document edit clears redo; presentation-only session controls and accepted final-content no-op batches do not necessarily clear it

Preserves file association/baselines, document generation, kept recordings/sweeps/viewer membership, viewport/pause and lifetime ID reservations. Undoing New/Open does not reassociate an older saved path or resurrect removed captured assets

Does not rewind numerical time/charge or jobs. Cancels pending input work; electrical/settings differences advance requested run/electrical revision and follow paused stale/restart rules, while geometry/presentation differences preserve accepted physics. Drawing references/selection may normalize when restored objects differ
Admitted history actions may affect eligibility of pending captured file/analysis work through their usual current-source guards; they do not roll back a publishing file or an external artifact

info.title: RC charge and discharge
info.question: How quickly does a capacitor charge and discharge?
info.expected: Capacitor voltage changes smoothly; switching from charge to discharge reverses current while preserving voltage at the switching instant.
info.try: Pause, step 10 ms, then choose Discharge. Increase R1 or C1 to slow the response.
info.limitation: Ideal capacitor/resistor with zero ESR and leakage; this example uses an ideal source edge.

value_domain.syntax: Bare SI or V; m/u/µ/μ prefixes, for example 500 mV or 1 V

matching_parts.limitations: Ideal DC voltage source; positive minus negative sets its voltage, and either terminal may be above/below ground in a referenced network. No output resistance, current limit, battery discharge, noise, heating, ratings or physical part identity.
matching_parts.name: DC source

value_domain.syntax: Bare SI or Ω/ohm; k/K/M prefixes, for example 2.2k or 0.1M Ω

matching_parts.limitations: Ideal constant resistance; no tolerance, heating, parasitics, ratings or physical part identity. Current is positive from pin 1 to pin 2.
matching_parts.name: Resistor

matching_parts.limitations: Educational generic diode; no physical part identity, reverse breakdown, thermal dynamics, ratings, or calibrated brightness.
matching_parts.name: Red LED

value_domain.syntax: Bare SI or F; p/n/u/µ/μ/m prefixes, for example 1 µF or 100nF

matching_parts.limitations: Ideal capacitor with configurable initial voltage; no ESR, leakage, polarity, heating, ratings or physical part identity. Voltage and current use pin 1 relative to pin 2.
matching_parts.name: Capacitor

value_domain.syntax: Bare SI or H; n/u/µ/μ/m prefixes, for example 10 mH or 100uH

matching_parts.limitations: Ideal constant inductance with configurable signed initial current; voltage pin 1 minus pin 2, current into pin 1/out of pin 2, energy L I² / 2. No winding resistance, saturation, mutual coupling, parasitic capacitance, heating, ratings or physical part identity. Add external resistance and a return path for switching current.
matching_parts.name: Inductor

value_domain.syntax: Bare SI or V; m/u/µ/μ prefixes, for example 500 mV or 1 V
value_domain.relation: Amplitude plus the absolute offset must be ≤12 V.

matching_parts.limitations: Ideal grounded voltage sources with per-component periodic sine or linear pulse ramps. No output resistance, current limit, battery discharge, noise or physical generator identity. Finite pulse high/low phase lengths include rise/fall respectively. Output sampling can alias; internal integration resolves waveform features within its work budget.
matching_parts.name: Sine source

value_domain.syntax: Bare SI or V; m/u/µ/μ prefixes, for example 500 mV or 1 V
value_domain.relation: High level must be at least the current low level (factory: 0 V).

matching_parts.limitations: Ideal grounded voltage sources with per-component periodic sine or linear pulse ramps. No output resistance, current limit, battery discharge, noise or physical generator identity. Finite pulse high/low phase lengths include rise/fall respectively. Output sampling can alias; internal integration resolves waveform features within its work budget.
matching_parts.name: Finite pulse source

value_domain.syntax: Bare SI or V; m/u/µ/μ prefixes, for example 500 mV or 1 V

matching_parts.limitations: Ideal square source with instantaneous edges and shared experiment phase timing; no output resistance, current limit, noise, ratings or physical part identity.
matching_parts.name: Pulse source

matching_parts.limitations: Generic enhancement PMOS with square-law channel, channel-length modulation and drain-to-source body diode. Body tied to source; zero gate current. No subthreshold conduction, body effect, gate/junction capacitance, charge storage, switching loss, breakdown, heating, ratings or named device identity. External capacitors provide circuit timing. Same illustrative beta magnitude as the generic NMOS, not a physical matched pair.
matching_parts.name: P-channel MOSFET

matching_parts.limitations: Generic enhancement NMOS with square-law channel, channel-length modulation and source-to-drain body diode. Body tied to source; zero gate current. No subthreshold conduction, body effect, gate/junction capacitance, charge storage, switching loss, breakdown, heating, ratings or named device identity. External capacitors provide circuit timing.
matching_parts.name: N-channel MOSFET

matching_parts.limitations: Educational Ebers–Moll DC model; no named physical device, breakdown, Early effect, heating, junction capacitance or switching delay. LED reverse current is neglected. Supports a grounded-emitter switch only.
matching_parts.name: NPN transistor

matching_parts.limitations: Generic five-pin educational macromodel with differential input resistance, midpoint-centered soft voltage limiting, finite output resistance, bounded active output current, supply-dependent enable and explicit supply currents. A declared 1 Gohm output-to-V- bleed remains with power off or reversed; differential input resistance also remains. No internal bandwidth, slew rate, offset/bias mismatch, common-mode restrictions, protection diodes, noise, thermal behavior, ratings or named physical device. External storage supplies circuit timing; this model cannot qualify physical amplifier speed or stability.
matching_parts.name: Powered op-amp

matching_parts.limitations: Common zero-volt reference; this symbol establishes the simulation reference, not protective earth or a physical grounding design.
matching_parts.name: Ground

matching_parts.limitations: Explicit electrical join; geometry/crossings alone do not connect wires. This helper has no physical device model.
matching_parts.name: Junction

matching_parts.limitations: Exact case-sensitive names join attached nets. A name alone never establishes ground. This helper has no physical device model.
matching_parts.name: Net label

value_domain.syntax: Bare SI or Ω/ohm; k/K/M prefixes, for example 2.2k or 0.1M Ω

matching_parts.limitations: Generic linear three-pin resistive track. Total resistance is split into two segments, each with 1 ohm endpoint resistance. Position 0 is toward pin 2; position 1 is toward pin 1. No contact noise, nonlinear taper, ratings, heating or physical part identity.
matching_parts.name: Potentiometer

matching_parts.limitations: Generic silicon junction with Shockley forward/reverse leakage and finite series resistance; no reverse breakdown, capacitance, charge storage, thermal dynamics, ratings or physical part identity.
matching_parts.name: Silicon diode

matching_parts.limitations: Generic SPST with finite on/off resistance; no contact bounce, arcing, thermal behavior, ratings or named physical part. Actuation is instantaneous; capacitor voltage remains continuous.
matching_parts.name: SPST switch

model.limitations: Educational generic diode; no physical part identity, reverse breakdown, thermal dynamics, ratings, or calibrated brightness.

info.title: RC charge and discharge
info.question: How quickly does a capacitor charge and discharge?
info.expected: Capacitor voltage changes smoothly; switching from charge to discharge reverses current while preserving voltage at the switching instant.
info.try: Pause, step 10 ms, then choose Discharge. Increase R1 or C1 to slow the response.
info.limitation: Ideal capacitor/resistor with zero ESR and leakage; this example uses an ideal source edge.

info.question: How quickly does a capacitor charge and discharge?
info.expected: Capacitor voltage changes smoothly; switching from charge to discharge reverses current while preserving voltage at the switching instant.
info.try: Pause, step 10 ms, then choose Discharge. Increase R1 or C1 to slow the response.
info.limitation: Ideal capacitor/resistor with zero ESR and leakage; this example uses an ideal source edge.
